title: 新版前言（黑兹尔·V. 卡比）

children: History is the fruit of power, but power itself is never so transparent that its analysis becomes superfluous. The ultimate mark of power may be its invisibility; the ultimate challenge, the exposition of its roots. —Michel-Rolph Trouillot
历史是权力的果实，但权力本身从来不是透明到无需分析的地步。权力最深刻的标记或许是它的不可见；而最艰巨的挑战，则是揭示它的根柢。——米歇尔-罗尔夫·特鲁约

en: It is the spring of 2013. The sun is streaming in through the windows of the Yale University Art Gallery where I am standing with a colleague, Laura Wexler. We're waiting for faculty and students to gather for a session we are about to teach in a new course for all students in the PhD program in American Studies: a practical forum on incorporating interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary methods, perspectives, and analyses into their scholarship. Two professors run the course, one an anthropologist and the other a historian. Laura and I are regarded as cultural-studies types, so following the sessions "In the Field" and "About the Archive," Laura and I are responsible for the session entitled "With the Texts." In the study gallery we are surrounded by the artwork on exhibit for our respective undergraduate courses that semester out of which we have each chosen one item for the graduate students in the research seminar to study. I have selected Ellen Gallagher's sixty-component print Deluxe (2004-2005), which dominates one entire wall; Laura has chosen a gorgeous gelatin silver print by An-My Lê, Rescue, from the series Small Wars (1999-2002).
zh: 那是2013年春天。阳光透过耶鲁大学美术馆的窗户倾泻进来，我和同事劳拉·韦克斯勒正站在那里。我们在等候师生们聚齐，好开始一门新课中的一讲——这门课面向美国研究博士项目的全体学生，是一个实践论坛，教他们如何把跨学科与多学科的方法、视角和分析融入自己的研究。课程由两位教授主持，一位是人类学家，一位是历史学家。劳拉和我被视为文化研究一路的学者，所以在“在田野中”和“关于档案”两讲之后，由我们两人负责题为“与文本同行”的一讲。研学展厅里陈列着我们各自本科课程该学期展出的艺术品，我们被这些作品环绕，并各自从中挑出一件，供研讨课上的研究生研习。我选的是埃伦·加拉格尔由六十个部件组成的版画《豪华》（Deluxe，2004—2005），它占满了一整面墙；劳拉选的则是黎安美（An-My Lê）系列作品《小战争》（Small Wars，1999—2002）中一幅精美的明胶银盐照片《救援》（Rescue）。

en: What has Michel-Rolph Trouillot's Silencing the Past: Power and the Production of History to do with these stunning works of art? Everything. When teaching in different spheres of knowledge and across different geographies, it can be difficult for two faculty members to agree on a particular reading for a class they are teaching together. However, Laura and I agreed immediately and simultaneously that the one book we wanted all members of the seminar to read not just for our session but also to purchase for their own reading and rereading was Silencing the Past. Our objective was to make our students think across the problems of "the field," "the archive," and "the text"; to enable them to understand the politics of representation, the complexities and subtleties of the relation between what they were reading and seeing, and to comprehend the nature of that relation as a relation of power. For, as Trouillot argues, "Historical representations—be they books, commercial exhibits or public commemorations—cannot be conceived only as vehicles for the transmission of knowledge. They must establish some relation to that knowledge."
zh: 米歇尔-罗尔夫·特鲁约的《让过去沉默：权力与历史的生产》与这些令人惊叹的艺术品有什么关系？关系无处不在。当两位教师分属不同的知识领域、又身处不同的地域，要为他们合上的课选定某一本共读读物，往往很难达成一致。然而劳拉和我不约而同、当即认定：我们要让研讨课全体成员阅读的那本书——不仅为我们这一讲而读，还要他们自己买来反复阅读的那本书——就是《让过去沉默》。我们的目的，是让学生贯通地思考“田野”“档案”与“文本”这三组问题；使他们理解表征的政治，理解他们所读与所见之间关系的复杂与微妙，并领会这种关系的实质是一种权力关系。因为正如特鲁约所论：“历史表征——无论是书籍、商业展览还是公共纪念活动——都不能仅仅被设想为传递知识的载体。它们必须与那种知识建立某种关系。”

en: Many scholars have celebrated the contributions of Michel-Rolph Trouillot to the fields of anthropology and history, as well as to intellectual thought in Caribbean studies and to theories of globalization. I draw an anecdote from my classroom to stress that Trouillot's work has relevance, influence, and intellectual power beyond these disciplinary and critical frameworks. His forensic analysis of the four moments when silences enter the production of history reveals an entanglement of historicity with power that applies not only in the archives but also dominates the processes and practices by which pastness is authenticated, ratified, and organized into fields of knowledge. For Trouillot, history is always material; it begins with bodies and artifacts, agents, actors, and subjects. His emphasis on process, production, and narration looks to the many sites where history is produced: the academy, the media, and the mobilization of popular histories by a variety of participants.
zh: 许多学者已经颂扬过米歇尔-罗尔夫·特鲁约对人类学和历史学两个领域的贡献，以及他对加勒比研究的思想探索和全球化理论的贡献。我从自己的课堂上撷取一则轶事，是要强调：特鲁约著作的意义、影响和思想力量，超出了这些学科与批评框架之外。他对沉默进入历史生产的四个时刻所作的缜密剖析，揭示出历史性同权力的纠缠；这种纠缠不仅存在于档案之中，还支配着过去性得以认证、批准并被组织成知识领域的那些过程与实践。对特鲁约来说，历史始终是物质性的；它始于身体与器物，始于能动者、行动者与主体。他对过程、生产和叙述的强调，着眼于历史得以生产的众多场所：学院、媒体，以及形形色色参与者对通俗历史的动员。

en: What history is matters less to Trouillot than how history works. The production of historical narrative, he argues, should not be studied as a mere chronology of its silences. In the pages of Silencing the Past we learn how to identify that what appears to be consensus actually masks a history of conflicts; we learn that silences appear in the interstices of these conflicts between narrators, past and present. There are many forms of pastness in Silencing. The book opens with an act of memory, which locates Trouillot in a very particular time and locale, a family, a community, a place: Haiti under the terror of the Duvaliers, where he learned that people can be "complaisant hostages of the pasts they create." It closes with Trouillot considering how "history works in a country with the lowest literacy rate on this side of the Atlantic," after witnessing an angry crowd taking a statue of Columbus and throwing it into the sea.
zh: 比起历史是什么，特鲁约更关心历史如何运作。他主张，对历史叙述的生产的研究，不应只是把其中的沉默排成一部编年史。在《让过去沉默》的字里行间，我们学会辨认：看似共识的东西，实际上掩盖着一部冲突史；我们懂得，沉默出现在古往今来的叙述者彼此冲突的缝隙里。《让过去沉默》中的过去性有多种形态。这本书以一次记忆行为开篇，把特鲁约安置在一个非常具体的时间与地点、一个家庭、一个社群、一个地方：杜瓦利埃家族恐怖统治下的海地。在那里他懂得，人可能成为“自己所创造的那些过去的温顺人质”。全书收尾处，特鲁约在目睹愤怒的人群把一尊哥伦布雕像扔进大海之后，思考“历史在大西洋此岸识字率最低的国家里如何运作”。

en: Silencing the Past has been required reading for my students since it was first published in 1995, and I refer to it continually in my own work. My only regret is that I never met Michel-Rolph Trouillot in person. But I have his words, his provocative questions, his insights, and they prick my conscience if I ever feel satisfied with just "imagin[ing] the lives under the mortar," remembering that Trouillot also asks how we "recognize the end of a bottomless silence."
zh: 自1995年初版以来，《让过去沉默》一直是我学生的必读书，我自己的研究也不断引用它。我唯一的遗憾，是从未与米歇尔-罗尔夫·特鲁约本人谋面。但我拥有他的文字、他那咄咄逼人的问题、他的洞见；每当我满足于只是“想象灰泥之下那些人的生平”时，它们便刺痛我的良知，提醒我特鲁约还追问过：我们如何“辨认一场无底沉默的终结”。

en: What is at stake in pastness for Trouillot is the future, the process of becoming. Silencing the Past provides strategies for countering inequalities of power in knowledge of the past. We learn how scanty evidence can be repositioned to generate new narratives, how silences can be made to speak for themselves to confront inequalities of power in the production of sources, archives, and narratives. We need to make these silences speak and, in the process, lay claim to the future. For, as Trouillot warns, "While some of us debate what history is or was, others take it into their own hands."
zh: 对特鲁约而言，过去性中利害攸关的是未来，是生成的过程。《让过去沉默》提供了种种策略，用以对抗关于过去的知识中的权力不平等。我们从中学习：稀薄的证据如何被重新安置，以生成新的叙述；沉默如何被要求自行开口，以直面史料、档案与叙述生产中的权力不平等。我们需要让这些沉默发声，并在此过程中申索未来。因为正如特鲁约所警告的：“当我们中的一些人还在争论历史是什么、曾经是什么时，另一些人已经把历史抓到了自己手里。”
